key_insight: SpikeDS uses dual sparsity—fewer spikes and fewer active 3D windows—to make spiking transformer MRI analysis more efficient while preserving diagnostic signal for PNI prediction.
clinical_relevance: This could support more practical 3D MRI-based risk stratification for cholangiocarcinoma patients by reducing compute and energy demands without sacrificing performance.
method: Binary spike communication reduces activation cost.
Window-based Expert Mixture Spiking Attention prunes low-firing windows and focuses attention on salient regions.
Cross-Window Spiking Self-Attention lets pruned windows still contribute as key-value sources for global context.
evidence_signal: In a 139-patient cholangiocarcinoma cohort with 5-fold cross-validation, the model achieved AUC 0.753 and used 14.4 mJ, outperforming the best baseline on both accuracy and energy efficiency.
watch_item: Single-center-style retrospective cohort size is modest, so external validation is needed before any real-world clinical deployment.
paper_title: SpikeDS: Dual Sparsity Spikformer for Perineural Invasion Prediction in 3D MRI
